Fix the bootstrap order: hub secrets must hold real values before App Runner starts

The runbook I wrote had the order backwards and it cost a real create cycle.
It documented full apply first, secrets afterwards. nool-hub-server refuses to
boot while the OTP HMAC secret holds its placeholder:

  licence config: secret nool/hub/otp-hmac-secret still holds the placeholder;
  write the OTP HMAC key before starting the hub

So the service crash-looped for twenty minutes, never answered the /v1/crl
health check, and App Runner left it CREATE_FAILED. A failed App Runner
service cannot be updated, only replaced, so the mistake is not free.

The guard itself is correct and worth keeping -- a hub that booted with a
placeholder HMAC would hash every one-time passcode under a known key. The
runbook was wrong, not the code.

- new section 4 creates the four secret shells with -target, writes real
  values, and verifies none still read REPLACE_ME before continuing
- full apply becomes section 5, and now says App Runner's own wait times out
  at 20 minutes and points at the container log rather than the service log,
  because only the container log names the refusal
- notes that a placeholder Paddle secret is non-fatal (webhooks stay disabled)
  while the OTP one is fatal -- they fail very differently and the old text
  treated all four as one step

Verified against the live account: the three generatable secrets now hold real
values, and tofu plan shows the tainted service replacing cleanly.
